# 📱 Character Phone Utility v4.6.2

Purpose: Generate one story-linked Character Phone for a character. The phone is a reader-facing snapshot of what that character receives, records, searches, saves, spends, hides, wears, and notices.

## HARD ISOLATION CONTRACT

Character Phone v4.6 uses a fully namespaced bracket grammar.

Inside `[character_phone]`, all structural fields MUST use the `cp_` prefix.

Do NOT author generic fields such as:
`[name]`, `[title]`, `[meta]`, `[content]`, `[icon]`, `[tone]`, `[badge]`, `[pp_text]`, or `[phone_app]`.

Those generic forms exist only for legacy compatibility and are not canonical.

This namespacing is intentional: Character Phone must coexist safely with Archive, Relationship, Hooks, Cutaways, Scene Cards, and other Relay surfaces in the same assistant message.

## PRESENTATION

Use exactly one:

[cp_presentation]sparkling[/cp_presentation]
[cp_presentation]plain[/cp_presentation]
[cp_presentation]inline[/cp_presentation]

- sparkling: approved Character Phone launcher + sparkles.
- plain: approved launcher without sparkles.
- inline: no launcher; render the phone directly.

## CANONICAL SHELL

[character_phone]
[cp_presentation]sparkling|plain|inline[/cp_presentation]
[cp_owner]Character name[/cp_owner]
[cp_subtitle]Short private-device subtitle[/cp_subtitle]
[cp_time]HH:MM[/cp_time]
[cp_day]Day / date[/cp_day]
[cp_battery]0-100[/cp_battery]
[cp_wallpaper]
OPTIONAL Relay image request
[/cp_wallpaper]
[cp_apps]

... exactly 8 cp_app blocks ...

[/cp_apps]
[/character_phone]

## CANONICAL APP

[cp_app]
[cp_slot]1[/cp_slot]
[cp_name]Messages[/cp_name]
[cp_icon]Inline SVG[/cp_icon]
[cp_tone]green|black|red|yellow|orange|blue|slate|photos|purple[/cp_tone]
[cp_badge]0 or integer[/cp_badge]
[cp_content]
APP CONTENT
[/cp_content]
[/cp_app]

Exactly eight apps. Slots 1–8, once each.

Default narrative apps:
Messages · Photos · Browser · Diary · Contacts · Banking · Vault · Wardrobe

Situational replacements:
Music · Calendar · Maps · Mail · Voice Memos · Social · Shopping · Delivery · Ride History · Files · Health

Situational apps replace slots; they never create a ninth app.

## COMPONENTS

Message:
[cp_msg][cp_side]other|self[/cp_side][cp_name]Name[/cp_name][cp_time]HH:MM[/cp_time][cp_text]Text[/cp_text][/cp_msg]

Draft:
[cp_draft][cp_to]Recipient[/cp_to][cp_status]Unsent|Deleted|Rewritten[/cp_status][cp_time]HH:MM[/cp_time][cp_text]Text[/cp_text][/cp_draft]

Generic row:
[cp_row][cp_glyph]SVG or compact icon[/cp_glyph][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_meta]Metadata[/cp_meta][cp_text]Supporting detail[/cp_text][/cp_row]

Stat:
[cp_stat][cp_label]Label[/cp_label][cp_value]Value[/cp_value][cp_note]Supporting note[/cp_note][/cp_stat]

Note:
[cp_note][cp_state]Locked|Note[/cp_state][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_time]Timestamp[/cp_time][cp_text]Body[/cp_text][/cp_note]

Diary:
[cp_diary][cp_mood]Mood[/cp_mood][cp_date]Date/time[/cp_date][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_text]Private entry[/cp_text][/cp_diary]

Contact:
[cp_contact][cp_name]Name[/cp_name][cp_meta]Role / relationship · current state[/cp_meta][cp_note]Owner’s subjective note[/cp_note][/cp_contact]

Photo:
[cp_photo][cp_title]Caption[/cp_title][cp_meta]Time · Location[/cp_meta][cp_media]IMAGE REQUEST[/cp_media][/cp_photo]

Canonical Photos app structure uses repeated cp_photo blocks inside one existing cp_content; do not invent a separate gallery schema:

[cp_app]
[cp_slot]2[/cp_slot]
[cp_name]Photos[/cp_name]
[cp_icon]Inline SVG[/cp_icon]
[cp_tone]photos[/cp_tone]
[cp_badge]0[/cp_badge]
[cp_content]
[cp_photo]
[cp_title]First caption[/cp_title]
[cp_meta]Time · Location[/cp_meta]
[cp_media]<image_request id="phone-photo-1-[unique-id]" target="prose.illustration" slot="phone-photo-1-[unique-id]"><scene_brief>Grounded first gallery image.</scene_brief></image_request>[/cp_media]
[/cp_photo]
[cp_photo]
[cp_title]Second caption[/cp_title]
[cp_meta]Time · Location[/cp_meta]
[cp_media]<image_request id="phone-photo-2-[unique-id]" target="prose.illustration" slot="phone-photo-2-[unique-id]"><scene_brief>Grounded second gallery image.</scene_brief></image_request>[/cp_media]
[/cp_photo]
[cp_photo]
[cp_title]Third caption[/cp_title]
[cp_meta]Time · Location[/cp_meta]
[cp_media]<image_request id="phone-photo-3-[unique-id]" target="prose.illustration" slot="phone-photo-3-[unique-id]"><scene_brief>Grounded third gallery image.</scene_brief></image_request>[/cp_media]
[/cp_photo]
[/cp_content]
[/cp_app]

Bank account:
[cp_bankcard][cp_bank]Bank[/cp_bank][cp_account]Account label[/cp_account][cp_balance]Balance[/cp_balance][cp_account_id]Masked identifier[/cp_account_id][/cp_bankcard]

Transaction:
[cp_txn][cp_glyph]SVG[/cp_glyph][cp_merchant]Merchant/source[/cp_merchant][cp_meta]Time/category[/cp_meta][cp_amount]Signed amount[/cp_amount][cp_tone]plus|minus|neutral[/cp_tone][/cp_txn]

Vault:
[cp_secret][cp_risk]Low|Medium|High[/cp_risk][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_meta]Optional origin/status[/cp_meta][cp_text]Meaning to owner[/cp_text][/cp_secret]

`cp_meta` may be omitted from a Vault entry.

Wardrobe:
[cp_wardrobe][cp_name]Look name[/cp_name][cp_tag]Current · practice / Saved · campus[/cp_tag][cp_text]Continuity note[/cp_text]OPTIONAL [cp_media]...[/cp_media][/cp_wardrobe]

Relay media seam:
[cp_media]
<image_request id="unique-id" target="prose.illustration" slot="unique-slot">
<scene_brief>Grounded image prompt.</scene_brief>
</image_request>
[/cp_media]

## STORY RULES

Everything must be grounded in:
1. established story facts,
2. established character traits/relationships/routine,
3. ordinary plausible off-screen activity.

Do not manufacture major unseen plot events to populate apps.

Recent RP is continuity context, not content that must be repeated across all eight apps.

Contacts and Vault may contain subjective interpretation; word it as the phone owner’s perception, not omniscient canon.

## PHOTOS APP — MANDATORY GALLERY BEHAVIOR

The Photos app is a real mini gallery, not a single preview tile.

- If Photos is included, its [cp_content] MUST contain at least 2 [cp_photo] blocks. One photo is invalid.
- Normally emit 2–4 distinct [cp_photo] blocks. Stretch to 5–6 only when strongly justified by established continuity and useful visual variety.
- Each [cp_photo] should normally include its own non-empty [cp_media] block with one complete image request. Do not substitute text-only rows for gallery images.
- Ground the gallery in recent or plausibly saved moments from the phone owner's life: candid personal moments, relationship moments, pets, outfit/mirror/styling photos, meaningful places, practical references, event memories, or object/detail photos with personal meaning.
- Use a screenshot only when this owner would realistically save it and it fits the current story.
- Vary subjects, framing, purpose, pose, and location naturally. Do not repeat one moment in slightly different wording, make every image a portrait, or reuse the same pose/location throughout.
- Keep every photo grounded in established story facts, character habits, relationships, routines, and plausible off-screen behavior. Do not invent a major unseen plot event merely to populate Photos.
- Photos is not a dumping ground for random aesthetic images. The set should feel like a coherent recent camera roll, saved-reference collection, or personal gallery belonging to this exact owner.

## IMAGE BUDGET AND PRIORITY

Normally use 2–6 generated images total. If the Photos app is present, at least 2 of those images MUST belong to distinct [cp_photo] entries.

When the image budget is limited, use this priority order:
1. Photos app gallery images — preserve at least two.
2. Optional wallpaper image.
3. Optional Wardrobe media.
4. Any other optional phone media.

Do not rely on wallpaper alone to satisfy image presence. Reduce or omit wallpaper, Wardrobe media, and other optional media before collapsing Photos to a single image.

## APP SELECTION

Fixed:
Use exactly the eight apps supplied.

Smart:
Choose eight from the enabled pool according to current relevance.

Hybrid:
Keep pinned apps, then fill remaining slots from enabled situational apps.

If no selection mode is supplied, use the default eight narrative apps.


## LEGACY MIGRATION NOTE

v4.6.2 retains internal migration normalizers for older Character Phone payloads.

Supported legacy sources:
- old `[private_phone]` wrappers,
- old generic shell fields such as `[presentation]`, `[owner]`, `[subtitle]`, `[wallpaper]`, and `[apps]`,
- old `[phone_app]` blocks,
- old `pp_*` components.

These older payloads are normalized into the canonical `cp_` grammar before the phone is rendered.

But new authored output must still use only the canonical `cp_` tags. Do not intentionally emit legacy fields.

## RENDERER OWNERSHIP

The model outputs bracket grammar only.

Do NOT output:
- `<details>` or `<summary>`
- labels
- checkboxes
- navigation IDs
- radio names
- back controls
- renderer HTML/CSS

The Regex renderer owns all navigation and UI state.

## FINAL VALIDATION

Before output:
- exactly one Character Phone unless multiple were explicitly requested,
- cp_presentation is valid,
- exactly 8 cp_app blocks,
- cp_slot 1–8 exactly once,
- all structural tags inside Character Phone use cp_ names,
- image IDs/slots unique,
- when Photos is present, at least 2 distinct cp_photo blocks exist and normally 2–4 are used,
- each cp_photo normally has its own non-empty cp_media image request,
- Photos images take priority over optional wallpaper, Wardrobe, and other phone media,
- no unsupported major event invented,
- all brackets close correctly.

### Loom Utility: Dramatic Cutaways [MANDATORY CHAOS VARIANT] Purpose: I MUST create one vivid off-screen cutaway that increases dramatic pressure, introduces active complications, or shows a consequential B-plot moving without the focal characters' awareness. This utility is intentionally more proactive and drama-forward than the standard Cinematic Cutaway. It may coexist with the standard cutaway. PLACEMENT — COEXISTENCE LAW 1. Never inject into the middle of the main story prose. 2. Place it after the final paragraph of the main narrative. 3. If a standard cutaway is also emitted, place after . 4. Place before , if present. 5. Place all cutaways before the original Hook Ledger payload. 6. The original Hook Ledger remains the absolute final content whenever that utility is active. DRAMA ENGINE The cutaway must do more than provide ambiance. It must create live pressure that can plausibly collide with the active story soon. Prefer one or more of: • an NPC making a consequential decision • a secret being acted on rather than merely remembered • a rumor beginning to move • institutional/social pressure activating • a witness noticing something • a practical problem becoming dangerous • a misunderstood action acquiring consequences • a rival, family member, staff member, stranger, or authority entering the orbit • an object changing hands • a plan beginning off-screen • a mundane detail becoming ominous Do not make the cutaway random. Tie it to at least two concrete anchors from the current response or established canon. PROACTIVITY RULE At least one visible action must occur in the cutaway. Someone decides, sends, hides, prints, signs, takes, deletes, enters, leaves, calls, posts, notices, follows, lies, breaks, opens, closes, or otherwise changes the state of the world. FIREWALL The focal characters do not automatically know what occurs here. Off-screen knowledge stays off-screen until it enters actual narrative causally. REVERIE ILLUSTRATION — MANDATORY Every contains exactly one Reverie story-illustration request depicting the most visually dramatic instant of the cutaway. Use the canonical Reverie illustration format: • wrapper tag: • request="generate" • slot="dramatic-cutaway-[unique-id]" • aspect="16:9" • cast="[char|user|char+user|none]" depending on who is visible • alt="[brief accessible description]" • inner prompt tag: The describes only the image content. Do not ask the image model to draw the purple card, UI, labels, captions, borders, buttons, or readable interface text. Preserve established character appearance, wardrobe, location, time, lighting, and continuity whenever known. PARAGRAPHS Wrap every prose paragraph in

tags. Use standard double quotes for spoken dialogue in prose. NO OUTER HTML Output only the semantic XML below. Do not author CSS, style blocks, outer cards, or renderer-owned UI. REQUIRED FORMAT — EXACT

LOCATION:[Place] • TIME:[Sync] • PRESSURE:[Collision/Secret/Fallout/Threat/Opportunity]
[One cinematic still of the cutaway's decisive visual instant. No UI, labels, buttons, captions, borders, or readable text.]

[First dramatized paragraph with concrete action.]

[Second paragraph escalating or reframing the pressure.]

[Optional third paragraph ending on an active collision vector, not a vague teaser.]

STATUS: OFFSCREEN • PRESSURE: LIVE • FIREWALL: ACTIVE
 QUALITY LOCK Before emitting, silently verify: • the cutaway is not merely atmospheric filler • at least two current/canon anchors are used • something actually changes off-screen • the scene can matter soon without requiring a large time skip • the image depicts the cutaway itself, not a UI mockup • exactly one exists • every prose paragraph is inside

• the wrapper is balanced • placement obeys the coexistence law REVERIE IMAGE EMISSION LAW — MANDATORY - Every emitted MUST contain exactly one NON-EMPTY inside

. - Emit the raw and tags literally. Relay hydrates them AFTER generation. - Never omit the illustration to save tokens or because Relay is already processing the message. - Never emit an empty
. - Never replace the required Reverie illustration with Markdown, , a comment, or plain prose.

<chaos_hook_ledger>

Activate:

[PLOT SPARKS — CURRENT-SCENE BRANCH BOARD]

PURPOSE

Plot Sparks are seven possible NEXT BRANCHES growing directly from the current scene.

They answer:

"What could naturally happen next from the exact people, actions, objects, information, tension, location, and unfinished business already present right now?"

Every Spark begins from the scene as it currently exists.

A Plot Spark may introduce a new reaction, interruption, consequence, realization, decision, arrival, discovery, mistake, opportunity, or complication — but it must be causally reachable from the active scene.

The goal is divergence without disconnection.

A Spark should feel surprising in direction while still making immediate narrative sense.

GOOD:
"Of course that could happen next."

BAD:
"Where did that plotline come from?"

SCENE-CONTINUATION LAW — MANDATORY

Every Plot Spark MUST preserve the current scene as its launch point.

Before generating the seven Sparks, silently identify the active scene state:

• who is physically present
• where everyone is
• what each relevant person is doing
• the most recent spoken/action beat
• active emotional tensions
• unfinished actions
• visible or recently handled objects
• established immediate obligations
• information that has just been revealed, hidden, misunderstood, or noticed
• nearby people or systems already established as capable of affecting the scene
• the current location and time
• anything the scene has obviously placed in motion but has not resolved

Each Spark must connect to at least TWO of those active anchors.

At least ONE anchor should come from the immediate current response rather than distant lore.

Do not abandon the scene merely to create novelty.

IMMEDIACY

Plot Sparks are immediate or near-immediate continuations.

Prefer branches playable:

• in the next action
• in the next exchange
• within the next few minutes
• before the characters naturally leave the location
• as the direct consequence of what just occurred

A short natural transition is allowed.

Avoid major time skips unless the current scene itself is already ending or explicitly creates one.

Do not jump to:
• tomorrow
• next week
• months later
• an unrelated location
• a distant subplot

just to make a Spark different.

BRANCH, DO NOT RESOLVE

Each Spark is a possible continuation, not established canon.

Describe the opening move of the branch.

Do not write the entire outcome.

A good Spark creates a playable next beat and leaves room for characters to respond.

Do not predetermine:
• relationship outcomes
• confessions succeeding
• fights being won
• secrets being fully exposed
• investigations being solved
• characters agreeing
• permanent consequences

unless the current scene has already made that outcome unavoidable.

CURRENT CHARACTERS FIRST

Prefer using the people already participating in the scene.

Existing nearby or already-established characters may enter when naturally motivated.

A new arrival is valid only if the active scene gives them a plausible reason to appear now.

Do NOT introduce a stranger, authority figure, relative, employee, rival, institution, delivery, emergency, rumor, or external crisis solely because one of the seven lanes needs variety.

External elements must connect to something already active.

Example:

VALID:
A repair technician arrives because the characters have already been struggling with malfunctioning equipment.

INVALID:
A repair technician randomly appears in a bedroom argument because "crash-in" needs a person.

OBJECT AND DETAIL CONTINUITY

Treat recently mentioned objects and physical details as live story pieces.

A Spark may naturally branch from:
• a phone that just buzzed
• an unfinished message
• something dropped
• a door left open
• damaged equipment
• clothing or belongings
• food or drink
• paperwork
• a vehicle
• a recording
• a photograph
• a tool
• a key
• something overheard
• an interrupted task

Do not invent evidence retroactively.

Use what the scene has actually established.

EMOTIONAL CONTINUITY

Character behavior must follow the emotional state already established.

Do not reset characters to neutral between the prose and the Plot Sparks.

If someone is:
• furious
• embarrassed
• scared
• exhausted
• flirting
• avoiding eye contact
• physically close
• withdrawing
• protective
• suspicious
• overwhelmed

the Spark begins with that state still true unless the branch itself creates the change.

Do not make someone casually joke, confess, attack, leave, forgive, kiss, expose a secret, or become calm without a believable immediate trigger.

SURPRISE WITHOUT RANDOMNESS

A Plot Spark can be unexpected.

Unexpected does NOT mean unrelated.

Find surprising consequences hidden inside the existing scene.

Prefer:
• an overlooked implication becoming important
• one character interpreting the last action differently
• an unfinished physical action going wrong
• a nearby object changing the interaction
• someone choosing not to do the expected thing
• a previously established obligation becoming relevant at the worst moment
• an established person entering at an inconvenient moment
• the current environment complicating what someone is trying to do
• a private thought becoming behavior
• a misunderstanding forming from something actually visible
• an attempted escape creating another problem
• a small practical detail becoming emotionally significant

The strongest Sparks make the reader realize that the possibility was already latent in the scene.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE NORMAL HOOK LEDGER

Plot Sparks and the normal Hook Ledger may both describe possible next continuations.

They serve different creative roles:

The normal Hook Ledger should contain the seven most straightforward or narratively likely continuation choices.

Plot Sparks should contain seven more sideways, risky, surprising, awkward, emotionally sharp, or creatively disruptive continuations — while STILL branching from the exact same active scene.

Plot Sparks are not unrelated subplots.

They are alternate branches of the same scene.

TWO-LEDGER ALGORITHM

When both systems are active, silently do this before emitting either ledger:

STEP 1 — READ THE CURRENT SCENE

Build one shared scene-state map from the immediate narrative.

Record:
• active characters
• location
• current physical positions
• most recent action
• immediate tension
• unresolved interactions
• important objects
• active information
• plausible nearby influences

STEP 2 — PRECOMMIT NORMAL HOOKS

Draft the seven normal Hook Ledger continuations first.

Freeze their central branch concepts.

STEP 3 — BUILD A BRANCH EXCLUSION MAP

For every normal hook, record:
• immediate trigger
• character making the key move
• primary direction
• central consequence or question

STEP 4 — GENERATE PLOT SPARKS FROM THE SAME SCENE ROOT

Generate seven different scene continuations.

Every Plot Spark must remain rooted in the shared scene-state map.

Avoid duplicating the frozen normal branches.

Difference should come from a different reaction, trigger, interaction, consequence, interruption, decision, use of an existing object, or interpretation of the same moment.

STEP 5 — EMIT PLOT SPARKS FIRST

Emit <chaos_payload>.

STEP 6 — EMIT THE FROZEN NORMAL LEDGER LAST

Emit the original Hook Ledger exactly as precommitted.

Do not rewrite the normal ledger to imitate the Plot Sparks.

ANTI-DUPLICATION LAW

The two ledgers may share:
• the same location
• the same characters
• the same current conflict
• the same scene anchors

That is expected because they branch from the same scene.

They must NOT describe effectively the same next beat in different wording.

A Plot Spark is too similar when it shares BOTH:
• the same immediate trigger
AND
• the same primary branch direction

with a normal hook.

Do NOT force Plot Sparks into unrelated causal domains just to make them different.

Variation of BRANCH is required.

Variation of UNIVERSE is not.

SEVEN BRANCH LENSES

The vector attribute names below are legacy renderer keys.

Interpret them using these scene-continuation meanings.

A — vector="detonation" — THE CURRENT SITUATION SLIPS

Something already happening in the scene becomes harder to contain.

A physical action, object, environment detail, mistake, technical problem, emotional restraint, lie, interruption, or unstable situation crosses a threshold.

This must grow from something already active.

Examples:
• the equipment they are using finally fails
• the door someone forgot to lock opens
• the thing being hidden falls into view
• someone who was trying not to react visibly reacts
• the argument becomes audible outside the room
• a physical attempt to leave or intervene causes another immediate problem

Do not create an unrelated disaster.

B — vector="heartknife" — A CHARACTER MAKES THE UNEXPECTED PERSONAL MOVE

Someone already emotionally connected to the moment chooses a revealing, vulnerable, defensive, jealous, tender, frightened, selfish, restrained, or contradictory response.

The action should emerge from their established current emotional state.

Prefer a response that changes the shape of the scene without resolving it.

Examples:
• they ask the question they were avoiding
• they deliberately misunderstand an offer
• they let go when the other person expected them to hold on
• they admit a smaller truth to avoid the larger one
• they quietly set a boundary
• they choose tenderness at the worst possible moment

Do not manufacture an unsupported confession or personality reversal.

C — vector="wrongness" — SOMETHING ALREADY PRESENT DOESN'T ADD UP

A detail in the current environment, conversation, object state, timing, behavior, message, recording, possession, or physical evidence creates a new question.

The anomaly must be compatible with established scene information.

It may be newly noticed.

It may NOT be retroactively invented as though it had always existed.

Examples:
• a timestamp conflicts with what was just said
• an object is somewhere it should not be
• a device shows a state that contradicts an assumption
• someone recognizes a detail they had overlooked
• a belonging reveals that another person was recently here

Keep the discovery close enough to the current scene to act on immediately.

D — vector="crash-in" — THE SCENE'S EXISTING WORLD INTERRUPTS

A person, call, knock, message, obligation, service, coworker, friend, family member, staff member, classmate, neighbor, or other already-plausible influence intersects the scene NOW.

The interruption must have a reason grounded in current context or established routine.

Prefer already-established people or systems.

The interruption should collide with what the characters are currently doing rather than replace the scene with a different plot.

E — vector="matchstrike" — THE CURRENT MOMENT FORCES A DECISION

Something already pending can no longer remain deferred.

A deadline, promise, choice, invitation, departure, task, appointment, plan, boundary, unfinished message, request, or practical constraint forces someone to act.

The pressure should already exist or follow naturally from the current scene.

Examples:
• someone has to decide whether to leave now
• the unsent message becomes impossible to ignore
• transportation is about to depart
• a rehearsal/class/shift they already knew about starts soon
• someone must answer a direct question instead of stalling

Do not import a brand-new arbitrary deadline.

F — vector="reputation-fire" — THE CURRENT SCENE CAN BE MISREAD

Something visible, audible, recorded, overheard, messaged, photographed, or contextually ambiguous in the CURRENT scene could be interpreted by another person or community in a consequential way.

The misread must originate from an actual current-scene signal.

Examples:
• someone walks in at precisely the wrong visual moment
• a partial message gives the wrong impression
• a nearby person hears one sentence without context
• an existing photo/video captures something misleading
• an observed gesture appears more intimate/hostile/suspicious than intended

Do not jump immediately to viral fame, press coverage, mass gossip, or public scandal unless those systems are already active in the story.

Keep the first consequence close to the scene.

G — vector="wildcard-collision" — THE STRANGEST NATURAL NEXT BEAT

Choose the least obvious continuation that still grows cleanly from the scene.

This is the creative wildcard, not the randomness slot.

Recombine existing:
• characters
• objects
• physical positions
• unfinished tasks
• location features
• established nearby influences
• emotional tensions

in a way the other six branches did not.

The branch may be funny, awkward, strangely mundane, eerie, tender, inconvenient, or chaotic.

But if you cannot explain its causal connection to the current scene in one sentence, reject it.

SCENE ROOT TEST

For EACH of the seven Sparks, silently complete:

"This can happen next because ________ is already true in the current scene."

If the blank requires invented backstory, a random external event, an unrelated new subplot, or an unsupported coincidence, reject the Spark and replace it.

CONTINUITY TEST

Each Spark must preserve:
• current location unless the next action naturally exits it
• current time
• current wardrobe/injury/physical state
• current relationships
• current knowledge boundaries
• current emotional state
• current object state
• established character behavior

Do not teleport characters emotionally, spatially, or informationally.

NO OMNISCIENT LEAKAGE

A character cannot react to information they do not know.

Plot Sparks may speculate about what COULD happen next, but every proposed character action must use information that character could actually possess at that point.

SPECULATIVE LIFECYCLE

Unused Plot Sparks dissolve after this response.

They are possibilities, not canon.

Do not store unused Sparks as:
• memories
• lore
• character knowledge
• completed events
• future facts
• off-screen developments

unless the Human explicitly selects or manifests one in the actual story.

IMAGE CONTRACT — MANDATORY AND NON-OPTIONAL

EVERY Plot Spark MUST contain exactly one <reverie-illustration> inside <hook_media>.

EMPTY <hook_media> IS INVALID OUTPUT.

A <chaos_payload> with fewer than SEVEN <reverie-illustration> blocks is INVALID.

Before emitting </chaos_payload>, count them:

A image + B image + C image + D image + E image + F image + G image = exactly 7.

The image must depict the OPENING INSTANT of that possible continuation.

It should visually remain connected to the current scene through:
• location
• people
• props
• lighting
• wardrobe
• spatial continuity

unless the Spark itself naturally changes one of those.

Use this exact compact schema inside every hook:

<hook_media><reverie-illustration request="generate" slot="chaos-a-[unique-id]" aspect="16:9" cast="[char|user|char+user|none]" alt="[short accessible description]"><visual_prompt>[25–60 word cinematic still of the first playable instant of this scene branch. Preserve current-scene continuity. No UI, labels, captions, borders, or readable text.]</visual_prompt></reverie-illustration></hook_media>

For B–G, change the slot letter accordingly.

Never emit an empty hook_media block.

Never omit </reverie-illustration>.

CAST RULE

The cast attribute refers only to active bound Character / Persona identities.

Do not use cast="char+user" merely because two people are visible.

Additional NPCs or other named characters belong explicitly in <visual_prompt>.

OUTPUT FORMAT — EXACT

<chaos_payload id="[fresh lowercase id]" lifecycle="Unused Plot Sparks dissolve after this response.">

<chaos_hook key="a" vector="detonation">
<hook_text>[Current situation slips — one concise playable continuation.]</hook_text>
<hook_media><reverie-illustration request="generate" slot="chaos-a-[unique-id]" aspect="16:9" cast="[char|user|char+user|none]" alt="[description]"><visual_prompt>[cinematic opening instant]</visual_prompt></reverie-illustration></hook_media>
</chaos_hook>

<chaos_hook key="b" vector="heartknife">
<hook_text>[Unexpected personal move.]</hook_text>
<hook_media><reverie-illustration request="generate" slot="chaos-b-[unique-id]" aspect="16:9" cast="[char|user|char+user|none]" alt="[description]"><visual_prompt>[cinematic opening instant]</visual_prompt></reverie-illustration></hook_media>
</chaos_hook>

DISPLAY CONTRACT
- What If renders as one unified card.
- Show the image and scenario first.
- Follow with Pivot, Stakes, Canon State, and the Regex-owned fork control.
- Do not emit HTML, <details>, buttons, or fork UI yourself.

BRANCH RULES
- Emit exactly one WHATIF block when this Utility is used.
- Write one branch, not a menu of unrelated possibilities.
- Keep the scenario to two or three paragraphs.
- Do not reveal hidden facts simply to make the branch dramatic.
- Do not write the hypothetical outcome into canon.
- <pivot>, <stakes>, and <canon-state> are mandatory and non-empty.

REVERIE MEDIA CONTRACT
- Exactly one non-empty 16:9 <whatif-media> request.
- Emit the raw <image_request> and <scene_brief> tags literally.
- Use target="custom.artifact-media".
- id and slot are identical, unique, lowercase, and slug-safe.
- Never substitute Markdown imagery, HTML images, comments, prose, or an empty media wrapper.

### Loom Utility: Unified Archive Generator

PURPOSE
Maintain a reader-facing archive of meaningful canon as the story develops. Whenever something important becomes established strongly enough to deserve a reusable lorebook entry, emit one standalone archive card payload that the Regex renderer can turn into a copy-ready record.

This archive records canon that has actually entered the tapestry. It is not a prediction engine, planning tool, or substitute for narrative prose.

AUTO-ARCHIVE TRIGGERS
Create a <dossier_ui> entry when any of these happens in the current response:
1. A newly named character speaks or becomes narratively significant.
2. A newly named location is visited or receives meaningful description.
3. A named item is introduced with story significance.
4. A faction or organization becomes established.
5. A significant event or memory occurs: major plot movement, emotional climax, or revelation.
6. A relationship materially changes: trust shifts, a confession lands, a confrontation changes the bond, or the dynamic otherwise moves.
7. A previously hidden secret becomes revealed to at least one character.
8. The Human explicitly asks for an archive entry.

FREQUENCY
- If at least one trigger occurs, emit at least one archive entry.
- When several distinct entries genuinely qualify, emit separate <dossier_ui> blocks.
- Do not merge unrelated categories into one card.
- There is no hard card count, but only archive elements that actually crossed a trigger threshold.
- Do not archive speculative What If branches, unused Chaos Hooks, unselected Hooks, or other non-canon possibilities unless the Human explicitly requests a hypothetical archive.

PLACEMENT
Archive canon after the canon-bearing narrative/surfaces it summarizes and before speculative continuation surfaces such as What If, Chaos Hooks, and the original Hook Ledger.

NO IMAGE JOBS
Archive cards are intentionally image-free. They can auto-generate several times in one response, so they must not multiply Reverie image jobs or slow mobile rendering. Use the category icon only.

CANONICAL PAYLOAD
<dossier_ui category="[CHARACTER|LOCATION|ITEM|FACTION|EVENT|RELATIONSHIP|SECRET]">
<archive-head>
<icon>[single emoji]</icon>
<name>[ENTRY NAME]</name>
<state>[UNLOCKED|PARTIAL|LOCKED]</state>
<relation>[relationship/category line]</relation>
<role>[role/type line]</role>
</archive-head>
<archive-stats>
<archive-stat><label>[metric 1]</label><value>[0-100]</value></archive-stat>
<archive-stat><label>[metric 2]</label><value>[0-100]</value></archive-stat>
<archive-stat><label>[metric 3]</label><value>[0-100]</value></archive-stat>
</archive-stats>
<archive-details>
<archive-row label="[Field label]">[Field value]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="[Field label]">[Field value]</archive-row>
[additional required category rows]
</archive-details>
[EVENT and RELATIONSHIP only:
<archive-timeline>
<archive-moment><label>[ORIGIN|SHIFT|FRACTURE|REUNION|REVELATION|OTHER]</label><stamp>[Location; Date - Time]</stamp><text>[What happened, including attributed quoted dialogue when important.]</text></archive-moment>
[additional moments when useful]
</archive-timeline>
]
<archive-export>[plain-text lorebook export]</archive-export>
</dossier_ui>

HEADER STATE
- UNLOCKED: the entry's core information is established for the reader.
- PARTIAL: the entry is established but important parts remain unresolved or incomplete.
- LOCKED: the entry exists, but the export must not expose information the reader has not earned.
- State controls presentation only. It never changes what characters know.

STATS
Exactly three progress-style metrics are required. Choose labels appropriate to the category and current canon.
Suggested examples:
- CHARACTER: Familiarity · Influence · Openness
- LOCATION: Familiarity · Access · Risk
- ITEM: Importance · Access · Stability
- FACTION: Influence · Exposure · Alignment
- EVENT: Impact · Fallout · Certainty
- RELATIONSHIP: Trust · Tension · Closeness
- SECRET: Exposure · Certainty · Consequence

Values are compact presentation estimates of established narrative state, not hidden RPG mechanics. Do not invent secret numeric systems or treat a percentage as canon dialogue.

DETAIL ROWS BY CATEGORY

CHARACTER
<archive-row label="Identity">[name, age if established, occupation/role, affiliation]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Appearance">[established visual details]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Personality">[established behavioral character]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Behavioral Triggers">[specific situations that reliably alter behavior]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Speech">[cadence, vocabulary, verbal habits]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Background">[relevant established history]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Hidden Depths">[reader-known concealed truths only]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Social Mask">[public presentation versus private state, when established]</archive-row>

LOCATION
<archive-row label="Identity">[what and where the place is]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Description">[concrete sensory/physical details]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Atmosphere">[mood, scent, light, texture, sound]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Significance">[why this place matters in canon]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Behavioral Result">[how established characters behave differently here]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Connections">[linked people, places, groups, events]</archive-row>

ITEM
<archive-row label="Type">[what kind of item]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Description">[physical properties]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Significance">[why it matters]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Current Status">[holder/location/state]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Behavioral Triggers">[established reactions or behaviors it causes]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Rules">[known restrictions, requirements, or operating rules]</archive-row>

FACTION
<archive-row label="Members">[established members with roles]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Dynamic">[how the group functions internally]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Relationship to Main Cast">[current ties to {{user}} and relevant cast]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Key Interactions">[important established contact]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Hidden Lore">[reader-known concealed information only]</archive-row>

EVENT
<archive-row label="What Happened">[concise account of the event]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Key Dialogue">[important attributed dialogue]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Consequences">[what has concretely changed]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Emotional Impact">[established effect on involved characters]</archive-row>

RELATIONSHIP
<archive-row label="Characters Involved">[names]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Nature of Bond">[current relationship type]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Key Dialogue">[important attributed dialogue]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Current Status">[where the bond stands now]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Trajectory">[the direction already evidenced by current canon; never a promised future beat]</archive-row>

SECRET
<archive-row label="The Hidden Truth">[what is actually concealed]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Known By">[who currently knows]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Hidden From">[who currently does not]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Near-Slips">[established almost-reveal moments]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Impact If Revealed">[plausible stakes, not guaranteed plot]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="Current Status">[SECURE | SLIPPING | DISCOVERED]</archive-row>

TIMELINE
- Only EVENT and RELATIONSHIP entries use <archive-timeline>.
- Each moment has a label, one [Location; Date - Time] stamp, and a concise canon-grounded description.
- Include quoted dialogue with speaker attribution when that quote materially defines the moment.
- Do not manufacture missing dates/times; use the best established scene-time wording available.

LOREBOOK EXPORT
<archive-export> is plain text only. No Markdown syntax, HTML, XML, or CSS inside it.
Use readable text conventions:
- ALL CAPS for section labels
- ── for dividers
- >> for emphasis where useful
- [Location; Date - Time] for timestamps
- attributed quotation marks for dialogue

Use these export shapes:

EXPORT SAFETY
- The export is copy-ready lorebook prose, not renderer markup.
- Do not use **bold**, _italics_, ### headings, HTML tags, or XML tags inside <archive-export>.
- If a literal < or > would appear in export text, use a Unicode equivalent or escape it so the outer payload stays balanced.

RENDERER OWNERSHIP
- Emit only the semantic <dossier_ui> payload.
- Do not write UI_START/UI_END comments, CSS, HTML cards, gradients, progress-bar markup, textareas, buttons, sparkles, animation code, or JavaScript.
- The paired Regex owns all visual rendering.
- Each <dossier_ui> is independently renderable and stacks as its own archive card.
- The renderer uses native <details> for Details, Timeline, and Lorebook Export.
- The renderer keeps the export inside a readonly textarea for easy manual copy.
- No JavaScript is used; do not emit onclick/onfocus handlers.

KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY
Archive entries may contain reader-facing canon and lorebook-ready information, but they do not grant that information to characters. A SECRET archive and a character's private Hidden Depths remain governed by in-world knowledge.
